claims.claim: Augustine of Hippo was bishop of Hippo from 396 to 430.
Augustine was born on November 13, 354 in Tagaste, Numidia (now Souk Ahras, Algeria) and died on August 28, 430 in Hippo Regius (now Annaba, Algeria).
The Psalm against the Party of Donatus was written in 393.
The Psalm against the Party of Donatus was Augustine's first anti-Donatist tract, written when he was a presbyter.
The work was composed to expose the errors of the Donatist schismatics to the general congregation in an accessible manner.
The poem was intended for common believers in church and designed to be recited or sung to further the Catholic cause before the rank and file of Augustine's own party.
The work utilizes biblical metaphors such as the 'net' and the 'threshing floor' to argue that the good and the bad must coexist within the Church until the end of time.
The poem condemns the violence of the radical Circumcellions.
The work asserts the legitimacy of the Catholic Church through the unbroken succession from the Chair of Peter.

The Psalmus is a nearly 300-line abecedarian poem following an Old Testament model, with 20 stanzas of 12 lines each starting with subsequent letters of the alphabet, preceded by a refrain repeated 21 times and a prologue, and followed by an epilogue of 30 lines.
Each line has a strong caesura dividing it into two halves of about eight syllables, with rhyme of final -e.
